overview: This Senate resolution names July 2026 "National Anti-Counterfeiting and Consumer Education and Awareness Month." It highlights the role of trademarks, the brand names and logos protected under a 1946 federal law known as the Lanham Act, in helping shoppers know what they are buying. The resolution describes the dangers of fake goods sold online and in stores, such as counterfeit medicines, electronics, and cosmetics that may not meet safety standards, and cites federal seizure figures for fiscal year 2025. It supports public education efforts by government and businesses to help consumers avoid counterfeit products. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on July 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say counterfeit products can endanger people's health and hurt honest businesses, and that raising public awareness is one of the best ways to protect consumers.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it creates no new enforcement tools, funding, or legal protections against counterfeiting.
